actual_identity: BIP 110 — "Reduced Data Temporary Softfork" — IS real and IS the spam-filter proposal the user means. Author: "Dathon Ohm" <dathonohm+bip@proton.me> (pseudonymous; the BIP's Credits section says "Original draft and advice: Luke-Jr", so it is squarely from the Luke Dashjr / Bitcoin Knots anti-spam camp). Layer: Consensus (soft fork). Type: Specification. Status: Complete (BIP-3 process status, advanced 2026-06-25; number assigned 2025-12-03). It is a temporary, one-year consensus soft fork with seven rules that invalidate the main arbitrary-data embedding vectors (inscription envelopes, oversized pushes/witness items, bare-multisig-style large scriptPubKeys, big OP_RETURNs, taproot annex, huge taptrees, OP_SUCCESS). Deployment: modified BIP9, name "reduced_data", bit 4, 55% threshold (1109/2016), starttime ~Dec 1 2025, MANDATORY signaling blocks 961,632–963,647 (blocks not signaling bit 4 are rejected — URSF-style), lock-in no later than 963,648, max_activation_height 965,664 (~Sep 1 2026), active for 52,416 blocks (~1 year), then a terminal EXPIRED state. As of July 2026 it is in the STARTED signaling phase with near-zero miner signaling; Bitcoin Knots (plus Start9/Umbrel/myNode builds) ship enforcement, ~20% of listening nodes signal readiness (Lopp argues this is Sybil-inflated), and the mandatory-signaling window in August 2026 is the looming chain-split flashpoint. Note: BIP 110 shares its number slot with old 2015-era block-size BIPs (109 Andresen, 111 NODE_BLOOM) — the number was newly assigned in Dec 2025 under the BIP-3 process.

classification_rules.rule: Rule 1 — "New output scriptPubKeys exceeding 34 bytes are invalid, unless the first opcode is OP_RETURN, in which case up to 83 bytes are valid."
classification_rules.detection: For each vout: len(scriptPubKey) in bytes (hex length / 2). If first byte is 0x6a (OP_RETURN): noncompliant if total scriptPubKey > 83 bytes. Otherwise: noncompliant if > 34 bytes. Standard types all pass (P2TR/P2WSH = 34, P2PKH = 25, P2SH = 23, P2WPKH = 22, P2A = 4). This kills bare multisig data stuffing (Stamps: 1-of-3 fake-pubkey multisig ≈ 105 bytes) and uncompressed P2PK (67 bytes).

classification_rules.rule: Rule 2 — "OP_PUSHDATA* payloads and script argument witness items exceeding 256 bytes are invalid, except for the redeemScript push in BIP16 scriptSigs."
classification_rules.detection: Two checks. (a) Parse every script that executes (scriptSig, scriptPubKey, P2SH redeemScript contents, witnessScript, tapleaf script): any OP_PUSHDATA1/2/4 payload > 256 bytes → noncompliant. Inscription envelopes push content in up-to-520-byte chunks inside the tapscript, so classic ordinals fail here too. (b) Witness stack items that are script arguments (i.e., excluding the witnessScript/tapleaf script itself, the control block, the annex, and taproot keypath signatures) > 256 bytes → noncompliant. Exemption: the redeemScript push in a P2SH scriptSig, and witness/tapleaf scripts themselves, are scripts-not-data and unlimited in size (their internal pushes are still limited).

classification_rules.rule: Rule 3 — "Spending undefined witness (or Tapleaf) versions (ie, not Witness v0/BIP 141, Taproot/BIP 341, or P2A) is invalid. (Creating outputs with undefined witness versions is still valid.)"
classification_rules.detection: For each input, inspect the prevout's scriptPubKey: allowed = v0 (OP_0 + 20-byte or 32-byte program), v1 Taproot (OP_1 + 32-byte program), and P2A (OP_1 + 2-byte program 0x4e73). Spending witness v2–v16 or any other program → noncompliant. Also, in a taproot script-path spend the control block's leaf-version byte (first byte & 0xfe) must be 0xc0; any other tapleaf version → noncompliant. Requires prevout lookup (or the vin's prevout scriptPubKey if the decoder includes it).

classification_rules.rule: Rule 4 — "Witness stacks with a Taproot annex are invalid."
classification_rules.detection: For each taproot input with ≥ 2 witness stack elements: if the last witness element's first byte is 0x50, an annex is present → noncompliant.

classification_rules.rule: Rule 5 — "Taproot control blocks larger than 257 bytes (a merkle tree with 128 script leaves) are invalid."
classification_rules.detection: In a taproot script-path spend, the control block is the last witness element (after stripping any annex). Its length is 33 + 32·m; if > 257 bytes (merkle path depth m > 7, i.e., taptree deeper than 128 leaves) → noncompliant. Flagged tradeoff: this constrains BitVM-style giant taptrees.

classification_rules.rule: Rule 6 — "Tapscripts including OP_SUCCESS* opcodes anywhere (even unexecuted) are invalid."
classification_rules.detection: In a taproot script-path spend, decode the tapleaf script (second-to-last witness element after annex removal) opcode-by-opcode; if any opcode byte is a BIP 342 OP_SUCCESSx value (80, 98, 126–129, 131–134, 137–138, 141–142, 149–153, 187–254) → noncompliant. Must be a real script parse — bytes inside push payloads don't count.

classification_rules.rule: Rule 7 — "Tapscripts executing the OP_IF or OP_NOTIF instruction (regardless of result) are invalid." (The inscription-killer: targets the OP_FALSE OP_IF … OP_ENDIF envelope of CVE-2023-50428.)
classification_rules.detection: In the executed tapleaf script, any OP_IF (0x63) or OP_NOTIF (0x64) opcode → noncompliant. This catches every classic ordinals/BRC-20 inscription (OP_FALSE OP_IF 'ord' … OP_ENDIF), including tiny ones that pass the 256-byte push limit. Parse as opcodes, not a substring search.

classification_rules.rule: Grandfathering — "Inputs spending UTXOs that were created before the activation height are exempt from all of the new rules."
classification_rules.detection: If the prevout was confirmed before the activation height, rules 2–7 don't apply to that input (rule 1 always applies to newly created outputs). For a classifier without activation context, either ignore this or take activation height as a parameter and compare against each prevout's confirmation height. Rules are checked per-block only while the deployment is ACTIVE (52,416 blocks after activation), and mandatory bit-4 signaling applies to blocks 961,632–963,647.

summary: The user is right: BIP 110 ("Reduced Data Temporary Softfork", pseudonymous author Dathon Ohm, original draft by Luke-Jr) is the anti-spam camp's temporary one-year consensus soft fork, assigned Dec 2025 and now Status: Complete. It imposes seven rules on transactions in blocks while active: (1) non-OP_RETURN scriptPubKeys ≤ 34 bytes / OP_RETURN ≤ 83 bytes, (2) data pushes and script-argument witness items ≤ 256 bytes (P2SH redeemScript push exempt), (3) no spending undefined witness/tapleaf versions (only v0, Taproot, P2A), (4) no taproot annex, (5) control blocks ≤ 257 bytes (taptree ≤ 128 leaves / depth 7), (6) no OP_SUCCESSx anywhere in a tapscript, (7) no OP_IF/OP_NOTIF executed in a tapscript — the rule that nukes ordinals inscription envelopes. UTXOs created before activation are grandfathered. Deployment is a spicy modified BIP9: bit 4, only 55% threshold, mandatory signaling at blocks 961,632–963,647 (non-signaling blocks rejected), forced lock-in by 963,648, activation by ~Sep 1 2026, auto-expiry after ~1 year (EXPIRED state). As of July 10 2026 it's in the signaling window with negligible miner support; Knots/Start9/Umbrel ship it, Lopp and Core-side devs call it a Sybil-backed chain-split machine, and the August 2026 mandatory-signaling window is the countdown everyone is watching. A tx is 'BIP 110 compliant' iff every output passes rule 1 and every input passes rules 2–7 (modulo grandfathering).
notes: Caveats for the visualization: (a) 'Compliant vs noncompliant' is well-defined per-transaction, but consensus enforcement is per-block and only while ACTIVE — and rules 2–7 are waived for inputs spending pre-activation UTXOs, so a strict classifier needs activation height + prevout heights; a satirical one can just apply rules 1–7 flat. (b) Rule 3 and rules 4–7 need prevout scriptPubKeys / full witness data — use verbose getrawtransaction with prevout info. (c) Rules 6–7 require real opcode-level script parsing of the tapleaf; substring matching gives false positives on push payloads. (d) Fun classifier outcomes: ordinals/BRC-20 inscriptions fail rule 7 (and usually 2); Stamps bare multisig fails rule 1; big OP_RETURNs (Core v30 relaxed the datacarrier default to ~100KB, which is what provoked this war) fail rule 1's 83-byte cap; Runes' small OP_RETURNs typically PASS; plain P2WPKH/P2TR keypath payments always pass. (e) The BIP status is 'Complete' under the new BIP-3 process (spec finished, not deployed); reference implementation is a Knots-derived branch, and test vectors (bip-0110/test-vectors.json in the bips repo) exist if the user wants ground truth for the classifier. (f) News coverage attributing the proposal directly to Luke Dashjr conflates author and credited drafter — on-screen text should say 'Dathon Ohm (pseudonym), original draft: Luke-Jr'.
